en: veto; right of veto; right to refuse

examples.en: The president exercised his veto on this bill.
The permanent members of the UN have veto power.

examples.ko: 회의에서 한 명이 거부권으로 막으면 결정을 할 수 없어요.
examples.en: If one person blocks it with a veto in the meeting, no decision can be made.

examples.ko: 큰 결정은 엄마가 거부권을 쥐고 있어서 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: Mom holds the veto on big decisions, so it isn't easy.

examples.ko: 거부권 때문에 그 결의안은 통과되지 못했어요.
examples.en: That resolution couldn't pass because of a veto.
The National Assembly pushed back hard against the president's veto.

explain: 결정이나 법안을 막을 수 있는 힘이에요. 거의 '거부권을 행사하다'로 쓰고, 정치 뉴스에서 자주 나와요. 농담처럼 가족이나 친구 사이에서 '내게 거부권이 있다'고 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: When the government used its veto, the bill stopped.
phrases.nuance_ko: 거부할 수 있는 힘을 실제로 쓴다는 뜻이고 정치 뉴스에서 가장 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means actually using the power to veto; most common in political news.

phrases.example: 이 회의에서는 모든 회원에게 거부권이 있어요.
phrases.en: In this meeting, every member has a veto.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결정을 막을 힘이 있다고 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to explain that someone has the power to block a decision.

phrases.en: I have no right to veto in this matter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대할 힘이 없다는 뜻이고 농담처럼 말하기도 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means having no power to refuse; sometimes used jokingly.
phrases.en_equiv: to have no right to refuse

explain_en: It is the power to block a decision or bill, and it is almost always used as '거부권을 행사하다'. It appears often in political news. People also joke about having a 'veto' with family or friends.

en: to participate; to join; to join in

examples.en: I'll join this environmental campaign too.
Many citizens took part in the event.

examples.ko: 친구들이 다 동참하니까 저도 하고 싶어요.
examples.en: All my friends are joining, so I want to do it too.

examples.ko: 우리 반 모두 기부에 동참해 주세요.
examples.en: Everyone in our class, please join the donation drive.

examples.ko: 동참하고 싶은 사람은 손을 들어 주세요.
examples.en: Anyone who wants to join, please raise your hand.

examples.ko: 이 일에 동참한 분들께 정말 감사해요.
examples.en: I'm truly grateful to everyone who joined in this effort.

explain: '참가하다'는 대회나 모임에 들어가는 것이고, '동참하다'는 어떤 뜻이나 운동에 같은 마음으로 함께한다는 느낌이에요. 기부, 캠페인, 운동과 잘 어울리고 '~에 동참하다'로 써요.

phrases.en: I'll join you in that work too.
phrases.nuance_ko: '동참하다'와 비슷하고 말할 때 더 편하게 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 동참하다 and an easier word for casual speech.

phrases.en: Many people joined in the donation drive.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기부, 캠페인, 운동처럼 뜻을 함께하는 일과 잘 어울리는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A good pairing with shared-cause activities like donations, campaigns and movements.

phrases.en: Please join our environmental campaign.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람에게 함께하자고 부탁할 때 쓰는 존댓말 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite form used to ask others to join in.

explain_en: Join others in a cause or campaign (캠페인에 동참하다) '참가하다' is entering a contest or gathering, while '동참하다' means joining a cause or movement with the same spirit. It suits donations, campaigns, and drives, and takes '~에' (e.g., '캠페인에 동참하다').

dis.h: join others in a cause or event
gh: get involved, usually in something bad

p.n: 참여하다 is neutral participation; 동참하다 stresses joining together with others in a shared cause.

t90.ax: Many citizens took part in the event.

examples.ko: 경비가 물샐틈없어서 아무도 들어갈 수 없어요.
examples.en: Security is airtight, so nobody can get in.

examples.ko: 물샐틈없는 준비 덕분에 행사가 잘 끝났어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the meticulous preparation, the event ended well.
That team's defense is really airtight.

examples.ko: 계획이 물샐틈없다고 해도 변수는 생기기 마련이에요.
examples.en: Even if a plan is airtight, unexpected things are bound to happen.
Even the watertight guard had a small gap.
Lock up the doors tightly before you leave.

explain: '빈틈없다'와 비슷하지만 경비, 경계, 방어, 준비처럼 막거나 지키는 일에 더 자주 써요. 물 한 방울도 샐 틈이 없다는 비유라 느낌이 강해요. 일상에서는 가볍게 쓰기보다 뉴스나 이야기에서 꽤 힘줘서 말할 때 나와요.

phrases.en: Tight security continued around the venue.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지키는 일에 가장 잘 어울리는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural pairing for guarding.

phrases.en: He made a watertight plan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빈틈이 없는 준비를 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to praise a plan with no gaps.

phrases.en: The defense looks airtight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈에 보이는 느낌을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for how something appears.

explain_en: It is similar to '빈틈없다' (no gaps) but is used more for guarding or blocking things such as security, watch, defense and preparation. The image of not letting even a drop of water through makes it feel strong. It is less for casual talk and more for news or emphatic speech.

examples.en: Customers have the right to choose their menu.

examples.ko: 직원들에게 근무 시간 선택권을 주는 회사가 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: More companies are giving employees a choice of working hours.

examples.ko: 학생도 수업을 고를 선택권이 있어야 해요.
examples.en: Students should also have a choice in picking their classes.

examples.ko: 물건을 살지 말지 선택권은 소비자에게 있어요.
examples.en: The choice of whether to buy something belongs to the consumer.

examples.ko: 선택권이 너무 많으면 오히려 고르기 힘들어요.
examples.en: If there are too many options, it's actually hard to choose.

examples.ko: 내 삶의 선택권을 내가 갖고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to have the right to make choices about my own life.

explain: '선택'은 고르는 행동이고, '선택권'은 고를 수 있는 권리나 자유예요. '선택권이 있다, 선택권을 주다, 선택권이 없다'처럼 써요. 고를 방법이 없을 때는 '선택의 여지가 없다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: Customers have the choice of picking a drink.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고를 수 있는 자유가 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone is free to choose.

phrases.en: I gave my child the choice of picking a snack.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람이 고르게 해 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when letting someone else choose.

phrases.example: 저는 이 일에 대한 선택권이 없어요.
phrases.en: I have no choice in this matter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 고를 수 없을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you can't choose for yourself.

explain_en: The power or right to decide, given to someone (선택권을 주다) '선택' is the act of choosing, while '선택권' is the right or freedom to choose. It is used as '선택권이 있다', '선택권을 주다' and '선택권이 없다'. When there is no way to choose, people also say '선택의 여지가 없다'.

t90.ax: Customers have the right to choose their menu.

examples.ko: 소화전 앞에는 차를 세우면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not park in front of a fire hydrant.
There is a fire hydrant in the building's hallway.

examples.ko: 불이 나면 소화전 문을 열고 호스를 꺼내요.
examples.en: If a fire starts, you open the hydrant door and take out the hose.
I learned how to use a fire hydrant in safety training.
Parking is prohibited near the roadside hydrant.
Water was leaking from the hydrant, so I reported it.

explain: 불을 끌 물을 쓸 수 있게 만든 설비예요. 손으로 들고 쓰는 '소화기'와 달리, 소화전은 물과 호스가 연결돼 있어요. 길에도 있고 건물 안 복도에도 있어요.

phrases.en: Please don't park next to the fire hydrant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주차나 위치를 말할 때 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when talking about parking or location.

phrases.en: If there is a fire, you use the fire hydrant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불을 끄기 위해 설비를 쓴다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means using the equipment to put out a fire.

phrases.en: Know where the fire hydrant is in advance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안전 안내에서 자주 나오는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase often found in safety instructions.

explain_en: It is equipment that provides water for fighting fires. Unlike a hand-held '소화기' (fire extinguisher), a '소화전' is connected to water and a hose. You find them on streets and in building hallways.

examples.ko: 이 방은 열 명으로 인원이 제한돼요.
examples.en: The number of people in this room is limited to ten.

examples.ko: 사용 시간이 하루 한 시간으로 제한됐어요.
examples.en: Usage time was limited to one hour a day.
It's a place where entry is restricted by age.
Seats are limited, so please hurry.

examples.ko: 이 쿠폰은 한 번만 쓰도록 제한돼요.
examples.en: This coupon is limited to a single use.

examples.ko: 접근이 제한된 구역에는 들어갈 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't enter areas with restricted access.

explain: 수나 시간, 범위에 한계가 정해져 있다는 뜻이고 '~로 제한되다'처럼 '로'로 한계를 말해요. 규칙을 만드는 쪽에서 막는 느낌이라 '제한하다'와 짝이에요. 반대말에 가까운 말은 '무제한'이에요.

phrases.example: 제한된 시간 안에 문제를 풀어야 해요.
phrases.en: You have to solve the problems within the limited time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used to modify a noun that follows.

phrases.example: 이 도서관은 이용 시간이 제한되지 않아요.
phrases.en: This library has no limit on usage hours.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한계가 없다는 뜻의 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form meaning there is no limit.

phrases.en: Coffee is unlimited at this cafe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 제한이 없을 때 쓰는 반대말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite word, used when there is no limit.

explain_en: It means a number, time, or range has a set limit, and you state the limit with 로, like 열 명으로 제한되다. It feels like someone made a rule to restrict it, so it pairs with 제한하다. A close opposite is the noun 무제한.

dis.h: restricted by a rule or set limit
gh: limited to a set range or number
confined to one narrow area only

p.n: 제한 stresses a rule imposed; 한정 stresses the set range or amount.

t90.ax: Seats are limited, so please hurry.

examples.en: I haven't paid my local taxes yet this year.

examples.ko: 지방세는 구청 홈페이지에서도 낼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can also pay local taxes on the district office website.
If you buy a car, local taxes are charged.
The local tax bill came by mail.
Can I pay local taxes by card too?

examples.ko: 지방세로 걷은 돈은 지역 도로를 고치는 데 쓰여요.
examples.en: Money collected as local taxes is used to repair local roads.

explain: '국세'와 짝이 되는 말이에요. 자동차세, 재산세처럼 지역에서 걷는 세금이 여기에 들어가요. '지방세를 내다/납부하다'로 말해요.

phrases.en: I have to pay my local taxes by next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세금을 낸다는 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic collocation for paying the tax.

phrases.en: A local tax bill is in the mailbox.
phrases.nuance_ko: 낼 돈을 알려 주는 종이를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the bill that tells you what to pay.

phrases.en: Local taxes and national taxes are collected by different bodies.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짝이 되는 말로 둘을 비교할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as a pair when comparing the two.

explain_en: It pairs with '국세' (national tax). Taxes collected locally, such as the car tax and property tax, fall under it. You say '지방세를 내다/납부하다'.

en: to be punished; to be penalized

examples.en: If you break the law, you are punished.
That person was punished according to the law.

examples.ko: 규칙을 어긴 사람은 처벌될 수 있어요.
examples.en: A person who breaks the rules can be punished.
I heard that the employee who lied was penalized.
Please don't do it, because it's punishable.

examples.ko: 잘못이 없는 사람이 처벌돼서는 안 돼요.
examples.en: A person who is not at fault must not be punished.

explain: '처벌하다'는 벌을 주는 쪽이고, '처벌되다'는 벌을 받는 쪽에서 말해요. 법, 학교 규칙처럼 공식적인 곳에서 쓰는 말이에요. 일상에서 벌을 받을 때는 '벌받다', '혼나다'가 더 가벼운 말이에요.

phrases.en: Small mistakes are not punished.
phrases.nuance_ko: 벌을 받지 않는다는 부정 표현이에요. 규칙이나 법 이야기에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a negative form meaning no punishment is given. It is used for rules and laws.

phrases.en: If you lie, you can be punished.
phrases.nuance_ko: 벌을 받을 가능성이 있을 때 써요. 경고하거나 설명하는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when punishment is possible. It sounds like a warning or an explanation.

phrases.en: I got punished because I didn't do my homework.
phrases.nuance_ko: '처벌되다'보다 가볍고 일상적인 말이에요. 학교나 집에서 벌을 받을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is lighter and more everyday than '처벌되다'. Use it for punishment at school or at home.

explain_en: 처벌하다 is from the side giving the punishment, and 처벌되다 is from the side receiving it. It is used in formal settings such as law and school rules. In daily life, 벌받다 and 혼나다 are lighter words.

en: to rise; to prosper; to flourish

examples.en: Business went well and the shop prospered greatly.
They say a family that prospers has a lot of laughter.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 신제품 덕분에 다시 흥하기 시작했어요.
examples.en: Thanks to a new product, the company started to thrive again.
I hope my parents' shop prospers for a long time.
Rising and falling can happen in an instant.
The neighborhood that once flourished is quiet now.

explain: 반대말은 '망하다'이고, '흥하고 망하다'처럼 짝으로 자주 써요. 가게, 집안, 나라, 사업이 잘되어 번창할 때 쓰고 '번창하다'보다 입말에 가까워요.

phrases.en: I hope the business you just started prospers.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~이/가 흥하다' 꼴로 잘되기를 바랄 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '~이/가 흥하다' pattern is common when wishing someone success.

phrases.ko: 흥할 때도 있고 망할 때도 있다
phrases.example: 장사는 흥할 때도 있고 망할 때도 있어요.
phrases.en: Business sometimes thrives and sometimes fails.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말 '망하다'와 짝지어서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is paired with the opposite word 망하다.

phrases.en: The small shop flourished and opened more branches.
phrases.nuance_ko: '흥하다'보다 글이나 공식적인 말에 더 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: This fits writing and formal speech better than 흥하다.

explain_en: Its opposite is '망하다' (to fail), and the two often appear as a pair: '흥하고 망하다'. It is used for shops, families, countries and businesses that do well, and it sounds more spoken than '번창하다'.

t90.ax: Rising and falling can happen in an instant.

en: to build; to construct; to erect

examples.en: This company builds apartment buildings.
My grandfather built the house himself.
They will build a library next to the school.
It took three years to build.
You have to get a permit before building.
I want to build a hanok.

explain: '건축하다'는 집이나 건물처럼 큰 구조물을 지을 때 써요. '짓다'는 집, 밥, 옷, 이름까지 두루 쓰지만 '건축하다'는 건물에만 써요. '건축가'와 같은 말도 같이 알아 두세요.

phrases.en: We built a house in the countryside.
phrases.nuance_ko: '건축하다'보다 쉽고 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier and more everyday than '건축하다'.

phrases.en: A new school is under construction.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 짓고 있는 중일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something is being built right now.

phrases.en: The architect designs the building.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건물을 설계하는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the person who designs buildings.

explain_en: Formal; designing and putting up houses and buildings, construction wording. 건축하다 is used for building large structures like houses and buildings. 짓다 is used widely, for houses, meals, clothes and even names, while 건축하다 is only for buildings. Learn 건축가 (architect) along with it.

gh: build big works like roads or bridges
create land, a park, or a complex
everyday native verb: make a house
build and found, like a school or monument
build stone or earth structures, like walls

p.n: 신축하다 stresses that the building is brand new.

t90.ax: I want to build a hanok.

en: to be fixed; to be fastened

examples.en: The camera is fixed to the wall.
The injured leg was held in place with a bandage.
Once an idea is fixed in your mind, it's hard to change.

examples.ko: 월급이 고정되어 있어서 계획을 세우기 쉬워요.
examples.en: My salary is fixed, so it's easy to plan.
The screen is locked in place, so the text doesn't move.
The desk isn't fixed to the floor, so it wobbles.

explain: 나사·붕대처럼 흔들리지 않게 붙어 있을 때도, 생각·수입·역할처럼 안 바뀔 때도 써요. 붙이는 사람은 'A를 B에 고정하다', 붙어 있는 쪽은 '고정되다'예요. '고정관념', '고정 수입'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙어서도 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: I fix the shelf to the wall with screws.
phrases.nuance_ko: '고정되다'의 능동형으로, 붙이는 사람이 주어예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The active form; the person fastening is the subject.

phrases.en: I'm anxious because I have no fixed income.
phrases.nuance_ko: 매달 바뀌지 않고 정해져 있는 수입을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Income that stays the same each month.

phrases.en: If you drop fixed ideas, your thinking widens.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘 바뀌지 않는 생각을 말하는 단어예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A word for a way of thinking that does not easily change.

explain_en: State of being firmly attached or set, physical or fixed (책상 다리) Used both when something is held firmly in place, like a screw or a bandage, and when something does not change, like an idea, an income or a role. The person who fixes it says 'A를 B에 고정하다'; the thing that stays put is '고정되다'. It also appears in front of other words, as in '고정관념' (fixed idea) and '고정 수입' (fixed income).

dis.h: fastened or set so it won't move
gh: becomes stuck or entrenched, hard to change

p.n: 고착되다 means becoming stuck or entrenched over time, so it is unnatural for a shelf fixed to a wall.

t90.ax: The camera is fixed to the wall.

examples.en: The door creaked, so I oiled the hinges.

examples.ko: 자전거 체인에 기름칠하면 소리가 안 나요.
examples.en: If you oil the bicycle chain, it stops making noise.
My father oils his tools every weekend.

examples.ko: 기름칠해 둔 덕분에 기계가 잘 돌아가요.
examples.en: Thanks to the oiling, the machine runs well.
I learned how to oil it from a video.
Oil it in advance before it rusts.

explain: 기계나 문의 움직이는 부분에 기름을 바른다는 말인데, '기름을 치다'라고도 많이 해요. 기계의 녹을 막거나 소리를 없앨 때 써요.

phrases.en: After I oiled the door, it became quiet.
phrases.nuance_ko: '기름칠하다'와 같은 뜻으로, 말할 때 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 기름칠하다 and more common in speech.

phrases.en: Please grease the bicycle chain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부탁할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite request form.

phrases.en: You have to grease the machine to use it long.
phrases.nuance_ko: '기름칠하다'를 '명사+을 하다'로 풀어 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The same verb split into noun + 을 하다.

explain_en: You apply oil to moving parts of machines or doors, and people also say '기름을 치다'. It is used to prevent rust or stop squeaking.

examples.en: Thick pillars are holding up the roof.

examples.ko: 턱을 손으로 떠받치면 자세가 안 좋아져요.
examples.en: Propping your chin up with your hand makes your posture worse.

examples.ko: 무거운 짐을 어깨로 떠받쳐서 팔이 아파요.
examples.en: I held the heavy load up with my shoulder, so my arm hurts.
Small and medium-sized companies are the force that supports our economy.
The father caught the falling child with his arms.

examples.ko: 이 선반은 책을 떠받치기에는 너무 약해요.
examples.en: This shelf is too weak to hold up books.

explain: 무거운 것이 떨어지거나 기울지 않게 아래에서 버텨 주는 것이에요. '받치다'로 바꿔 써도 되는 때가 많지만, 경제나 가정을 지탱한다는 비유에는 '떠받치다'가 더 자연스러워요. 기둥 같은 실제 물건뿐 아니라 경제, 가정, 정권을 지탱한다는 뜻으로도 써요.

phrases.en: Small businesses hold up the national economy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경제나 가정처럼 큰 것을 지탱한다는 비유로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used figuratively for sustaining something big like the economy or a family.

phrases.en: I held up the falling box with my hands.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 아래에서 손으로 버텨 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when holding something up from below with your hands.
phrases.en_equiv: to hold up with one's hands

phrases.en: Two legs are holding up the shelf.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계속 지탱하고 있는 상태를 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows the ongoing state of supporting something.

explain_en: Physical: pillars or hands holding something up from underneath. It means supporting something heavy from below so it doesn't fall or tilt. '받치다' can often replace it, but for figurative use such as holding up an economy or a family, '떠받치다' sounds more natural. It is used for physical things like pillars and also for sustaining an economy, a family or a government.

t90.ax: Thick pillars are holding up the roof.
